facts.statement: The genus Gobivenator contains only one known species, Gobivenator mongoliensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Gobivenator mongoliensis.

facts.statement: Gobivenator mongoliensis is known from a single individual that represents the most complete Late Cretaceous troodontid specimen currently known.
facts.quote: G. mongoliensis is known from a single individual, which represents the most complete specimen of a Late Cretaceous troodontid currently known.

facts.statement: Gobivenator was first described and named by Tsuihiji et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: Gobivenator was first described and named by Takanobu Tsuihiji, Rinchen Barsbold, Mahito Watabe, Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig, Yoshito Fujiyama and Shigeru Suzuki in 2014

facts.statement: The generic name Gobivenator is derived from the Gobi Desert and the Latin word venator, meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the name of the Gobi Desert, where the holotype was found, and venator meaning "hunter" in Latin.

facts.statement: Gobivenator was discovered by a Japanese-Mongolian expedition.
facts.quote: It was discovered by a Japanese-Mongolian expedition, and represents the most complete specimen of a Late Cretaceous troodontid presently known.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from the Dzamin Khond locality in the Djadokhta Formation, dating to approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Dzamin Khond locality of the Djadokhta Formation in the central Gobi Desert, dating to the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 million years ago.

facts.statement: Unlike most troodontid fossils, the Gobivenator holotype is fully articulated and three-dimensionally preserved.
facts.quote: Additionally, unlike most troodontid fossils, MPC-D 100/86 is fully articulated and three-dimensionally preserved.

facts.statement: Gobivenator lived during the late Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in the central Gobi Desert, Mongolia.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Gobivenator mongoliensis. G. mongoliensis is known from a single individual, which represents the most complete specimen of a Late Cretaceous troodontid currently known.

facts.statement: Gobivenator was a small theropod measuring 1.7 meters long and weighing 9 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gobivenator was a small theropod, measuring 1.7 m long and weighing 9 kg.

facts.statement: Troodontids, including Gobivenator, possess sickle-claws and raptorial hands and are known for high non-avian encephalization quotients indicating advanced behavior and keen senses.
facts.quote: Troodontids have sickle-claws and raptorial hands, and some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, meaning they were behaviourally advanced and had keen senses.

facts.statement: Gobivenator provides detailed information on Troodontidae anatomy, supporting close relations with dromaeosaurids and basal birds like Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Gobivenator provides detailed information on many aspects of the poorly-understood anatomy of Troodontidae, including the morphology of the palate, supporting close relations with the dromaeosaurids and basal birds, like Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Although the skull of Gobivenator is akinetic, it possesses preconditions for the later evolution of cranial kinesis in birds, such as the loss of the epipterygoid bone.
facts.quote: Even though the skull of Gobivenator is akinetic, it already possesses preconditions for later evolution of cranial kinesis in birds, like the loss of the epipterygoid bone and a reduced contact areas between palate bones.

facts.statement: A 2024 study recovered Gobivenator as a basal member of the Troodontinae, as the sister taxon to Hypnovenator.
facts.quote: A 2024 study on Hypnovenator recovered Gobivenator as a basal member of the Troodontinae, as its sister taxon.

facts.statement: Gobivenator is classified as a Saurischian theropod dinosaur in the family Troodontidae and subfamily Troodontinae.
facts.quote: phylum: Chordata classis: Sauropsida superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Theropoda familia: Troodontidae subfamilia: Troodontinae

facts.statement: Gobivenator lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, 72 million years ago during the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 72 millones de años durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Gobivenator had a body length of approximately 160 centimeters, comparable in size to Saurornithoides.
facts.quote: Gobivenator tenía una longitud corporal de aproximadamente 160 centímetros, siendo comparable a Saurornithoides en tamaño.

facts.statement: Troodontids have sickle-claws and raptorial hands and some of the highest non-avian encephalization quotients, meaning they were behaviorally advanced and had keen senses.
facts.quote: Los trodóntidos tienen garras falciformes y manos rapaces y algunos de los más altos cocientes de encefalización no aviar, lo que significa que fueron avanzados en su comportamiento y tenían agudos sentidos.

facts.statement: Gobivenator has two unique traits distinguishing it from all known troodontids: fused parietal bones with a pointed anterior end and a fossa on the surangular bone of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Gobivenator posee dos autapomorfias, o rasgos únicos, que lo diferencian de todos los trodóntidos conocidos. Los huesos parietales están fusionados con un extremo anterior en punta, y una fosa se encuentra en el hueso surangular de la mandíbula, en frente del foramen posterior surangular.

facts.statement: Other potential unique traits of Gobivenator are the gracile build of the three postorbital branches and the elongation of the upper chevrons.
facts.quote: Otros rasgos son autapomorfias potenciales: la constitución grácil de las tres ramas postorbitales y el alargamiento de los cheurones superiores.

facts.statement: The skull of Gobivenator shows an elongated maxillary fenestra and an anterior lacrimal process much longer than the supraorbital process, features typical of troodontids.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Gobivenator muestra una alargada fenestra maxilar y un proceso anterior del lacrimal que es mucho más largo que el proceso supraorbital, rasgos que son típicos de los trodóntidos.

facts.statement: Gobivenator provides detailed information on the poorly understood anatomy of Troodontidae, supporting close relations with dromaeosaurids and basal birds like Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Gobivenator provee información detallada de muchos aspectos de la apenas estudiada anatomía de los Troodontidae, incluyendo la morfología del palatal, apoyando la cercana relación con los dromeosáuridos y las aves basales, como Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Gobivenator encompasses only one species, known from a single individual representing the most complete Upper Cretaceous troodontid specimen known.
facts.quote: Solo abarca a una especie, Gobivenator mongoliensis, conocida a partir de un individuo representado por el más completo espécimen de un trodóntido del Cretácico Superior conocido.

facts.statement: Gobivenator was originally named and described by Tsuihiji et al. in 2014.
facts.quote: Gobivenator fue nombrado y descrito originalmente por Takanobu Tsuihiji, Rinchen Barsbold, Mahito Watabe, Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, Tsogtbaatar Chinzorig, Yoshito Fujiyama y Shigeru Suzuki en 2014

facts.statement: The genus name is derived from the Gobi Desert where the holotype was found and the Latin word venator, meaning "hunter".
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del desierto de Gobi en donde se halló al holotipo, y venator que significa "cazador" en latín.

facts.statement: The species name refers to its occurrence in Mongolia, using the Latin suffix -ensis meaning "from".
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se refiere a su aparición en Mongolia, con el sufijo latino -ensis que significa "proveniente de".

facts.statement: Gobivenator is known from the holotype MPC-D 100/86, an articulated and nearly complete skeleton including the skull, housed at the Mongolian Paleontological Center in Ulaanbaatar.
facts.quote: Gobivenator se conoce del holotipo MPC-D 100/86, un esqueleto articulado y casi completo que incluye el cráneo, alojado en el Centro Paleontólogico Mongol en Ulán Bator, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype is mostly undistorted and well preserved, lacking only the snout tip, while the rest of the skeleton lacks only middle cervical vertebrae, forelimb bones below the elbow, some hindlimb bones, and most gastralia.
facts.quote: El cráneo de MPC-D 100/86 está en su mayor parte sin distorsiones y bien preservado, solo careciendo de la punta del hocico, mientras que al resto del esqueleto le faltan solo las vértebras cervicales medias, los huesos de las extremidades anteriores localizados bajo la articulación del codo, algunos huesos de las patas y la mayoría de la gastralia.

facts.statement: It was discovered by a Mongolian-Japanese expedition in the Dzamin Khond locality of the Djadokhta Formation in the Gobi Desert, dating to the Campanian stage approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto por una expedición mongol-japonesa en la localidad Dzamin Khond de la Formación Djadokhta en el desierto de Gobi, que data de la etapa del Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 72 millones de años.

facts.statement: Gobivenator was found to be an advanced troodontid closely related to other Upper Cretaceous troodontids such as Saurornithoides, Zanabazar, and Troodon.
facts.quote: Se encontró que Gobivenator es un trodóntido avanzado, cercanamente relacionado con otros trodóntidos del Cretácico Superior como Saurornithoides y Zanabazar de Mongolia, y Troodon de Norteamérica.
